transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I'm here because... well, I teach high school, and lately I just can't stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face on our lesson videos. 

It's really getting to me. Once I notice it, I just feel like the students, their parents, the other staff... I feel like they must all be staring right at it instead of actually listening to anything I'm saying.
How certain are you that this crooked, swollen appearance is truly noticeable to other people?

I'm completely certain. I mean, it's... it's right there on my face. When I watch those videos back, it's so obvious to me, so I don't see how anyone else could possibly miss it. It just feels like a fact that they're seeing it.
Do you still notice and worry about this appearance when you are alone and no one else will see you?

I'm... I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really noticed if I do. I mean, I think about it a lot in general, but I guess I don't know if I'm actively worrying about it when I'm just sitting by myself at home and no one is around. Mostly I just know how overwhelming it is when I have to be on camera or standing in front of the classroom.
How often do you check your face in mirrors, photos, or videos to see whether it looks crooked or swollen?

I do it a lot, actually. Um, especially before I post a recorded lesson or have to join a parent conference online. I just... I keep changing the camera angle, replaying the clips over and over to check how it looks. I'll sit there covering parts of my face with my hand, trying to see if I can hide it. Sometimes I end up re-recording the whole video so many times that I completely miss my prep work, and... well, I actually end up late for my classes because of it.
When trusted people or a clinician tell you they do not see noticeable crookedness or swelling, are you able to consider that they might be right?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I haven't actually talked to anyone about it. I haven't asked my friends or family, or even a doctor before today, because I just keep it to myself. So no one has ever really told me they don't see it. I guess I just don't know if I'd believe them or not if they did.
Is there any possibility that your face is not actually crooked or swollen and that your perception could be mistaken, or are you completely certain that the defect is there?

I... I don't know. I mean, I guess it's possible I could be mistaken, but... no, I'm just really certain it's there. When I look at the videos, it's all I can see. It feels very real and very obvious to me. I can't really imagine that it's just in my head.
Besides the belief that your face is crooked or swollen, do you currently have any other beliefs that people or events are connected to you in an unusual or threatening way?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like people are out to get me or anything like that. It's really just... just my face. That's the only thing that's bothering me. I don't have any strange thoughts about other things happening around me.
If I examined your face and told you that I could not see any noticeable crookedness or swelling, would you be able to accept that, or would you remain convinced that the defect is there?

I think... I think I'd still believe it's there. Even if you told me you couldn't see it, I just... I look in the mirror and it's so obvious to me. I know you're a doctor, but I'd probably just think you were missing it, or maybe trying to make me feel better. I'm just completely convinced that my face is messed up.
On a typical day, about how much time do you spend thinking about the appearance of your face?

I'd say... almost all day. It's actually why I'm here. I just can't stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face, especially when I have to watch my lesson videos back. Once I notice it, it's all I can focus on. It takes up so much of my time because I just sit there thinking about how the students, the parents, the other staff... they must all be staring right at it instead of listening to a single word I'm saying.
How long have you been preoccupied with the belief that your face is crooked or swollen?

I'm not exactly sure when it started, to be honest. It feels like it's been a while, but I can't really pin down a specific date or time when I first noticed it. It's just... something that's been on my mind for quite some time now.
When you repeatedly check, re-record, or cover your face, is your main goal to reduce distress about how your appearance looks to others?

Yeah, that's exactly why I do it. I'm just trying to make it so they don't see it. Like, before I post a recorded lesson or... or join a parent conference, I keep changing the camera angle to see if it helps hide it. I end up replaying the clips over and over, or just covering parts of my face with my hand while I'm on screen. Sometimes I re-record the whole thing so many times that I completely miss my prep work, and I end up being late with my classes. I just can't stand the thought of anyone seeing how bad it looks.
Has anyone else ever independently pointed out noticeable crookedness or swelling on your face?

No, no one has ever said anything to me about it. Not my students, not my colleagues, no one. I mean, they probably notice it, but they're just being polite and not bringing it up. But no, nobody has actually pointed it out to me directly.
Is your main concern that your face looks unattractive or abnormal to other people, rather than that you have a medical disease or physical injury affecting it?

Yeah, exactly. I don't think I have a disease or an injury or anything like that. It's really just... I can't stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face, especially when I'm looking at those lesson videos. And once I notice it, I just feel like the students, the parents, the other staff... I feel like they must be staring right at it instead of listening to anything I'm actually saying. That's what I'm worried about.
